newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-INTER'S MORATTI SAYS NO SIMONI DEAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTER'S MORATTI SAYS NO SIMONI DEAL.

text.p: Internazionale president Massimo Moratti denied media speculation that he intends to hire the current Napoli coach Luigi Simoni as a replacement for Englishman Roy Hodgson.
The speculation reached crescendo proportions on Tuesday evening following confirmation from Simoni that he will be leaving Napoli at the end of the season.
With Hodgson due to leave Inter for English premiership side Blackburn Rovers in June, some observers interpreted Simoni's forthcoming resignation as confirmation that he would be moving to Inter.

Speaking at the San Siro stadium after watching Inter qualify for the semifinals of the UEFA Cup by eliminating Belgian side Anderlecht on Tuesday, Moratti said: "The fact that Simoni has no contract with Napoli (for next season) doesn't mean that he has one with Inter."

Simoni has figured prominently in a long-running game of managerial musical chairs among serie A clubs this season, a game sparked off by the decisions of Swede Sven Eriksson to leave Sampdoria for Lazio and of Hodgson to move to Blackburn.
Simoni told reporters on Tuesday that the sticking point between him and Napoli had been his request for a renewed two-year contract.
Media reports said Simoni might settle for a one-year contract with Inter worth an annual $760,000 dollars as opposed to the $530,000 on offer from Napoli.

Simoni's prospects of landing the prestigious Inter job were further improved this week by the announcement that Atalanta coach Emilio Mondonico had signed a new three-year contract with the Bergamo club.
Mondonico, along with Simoni, had been shortlisted for the Inter job.
